name: Cold storage operators

problems.words: Client says he stored 500 bags, our register shows 470
quick_ideas: Count inward loads with the client or their representative present and both signing, so the starting figure is agreed
Give a receipt with the count every time.

workzap_build.text: An inward/outward register on phone by client account code, issuing a WhatsApp receipt with a unique code for every movement.

problems.ask_first: How is stock recorded when it comes in?
problems.free_stops: How receipts and codes are set up is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the inward register with unloading notes for the disputed lot once, so you can see exactly where the missing bags entered the paperwork.
Give one person the job of writing the final received bag count on the same inward page before stacking, so later disputes start from one figure.

problems.words: Stock taken out in parts and the balance per client gets confused
quick_ideas: Keep a running balance per client on its own page, so each part-release reduces a clear figure
Tell the client the remaining balance at every release.

workzap_build.text: A client stock statement sent on WhatsApp after every movement, showing what remains.

problems.ask_first: Do most clients take stock out in parts?
problems.free_stops: How statements are generated is part of the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many part releases for one client happened this week versus how many balance updates were written, so the balance confusion has a size.
Keep one balance page beside the release register and make the releasing staff update it before the vehicle leaves, so each client balance stays current.

problems.words: Bags end up in the wrong chamber and take hours to find
quick_ideas: Number every chamber and rack clearly, so each lot has an address
Write chamber and rack on every inward receipt.

workzap_build.text: A chamber and rack map showing where each client's lot sits, updated with every movement.

problems.ask_first: How many chambers do you have?
problems.free_stops: The map layout is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the chambers and note every lot found somewhere different from its written location, so you see which areas create the longest searches.
Give one shift one location notebook kept at the chamber entrance, so every moved lot gets one current written place.

problems.words: Gate passes are handwritten and can be copied
quick_ideas: Number gate passes in sequence and check each against the register before release, so copies stand out
Allow releases on one person's approval only.

workzap_build.text: A release flow where stock goes out only against a valid receipt code with an approval step.

problems.free_stops: How codes and approvals work is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this week's issued gate passes with the release register line by line once, so duplicate or missing paperwork stands out quickly.
Keep all blank gate passes with one responsible person only, so handwritten copies are harder to slip into a release.

problems.words: Rent collection at season end is a fight
quick_ideas: List every client's rent due with the agreed rate, so there is one record to point to
Share the balance with clients during the season, not only at the end.

workzap_build.text: Rent billing by season or month with balances and reminders sent through the season.

problems.ask_first: Is rent charged per bag for the season or monthly?
problems.free_stops: Billing and reminder setup goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which clients have no running rent note today and compare them with occupied space, so end season collection fights can be traced early.
Set one weekly time to update every client's running rent in one notebook, so collection talks start from one shared figure.

problems.words: Rates differ client to client and no one remembers what was agreed
quick_ideas: Write each client's agreed rate on their account page now, so it isn't from memory
Put the rate on every receipt.

workzap_build.text: Agreed rates stored per client account and added directly to every bill.

problems.ask_first: Do you have a standard rate list?
problems.free_stops: How rates link to billing is part of the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Check a few recent receipts against each client's account page once, so you spot where agreed rates are drifting in daily work.
Keep one rate list notebook in the billing spot and assign one person to update it after any agreement, so receipts follow the same record.

problems.words: Compressor failed at night and nobody noticed till morning
quick_ideas: Ask the night shift to send a reading and photo of each chamber at set times, so problems surface sooner
Keep a breakdown book for compressors and generators.

workzap_build.text: Connecting temperature sensors, where available, so the owner's phone gets an alert the moment a chamber goes out of range.

problems.ask_first: Do the chambers have any sensors now?
problems.free_stops: Which sensors connect and how alerts are routed goes in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the actual time each night issue was noticed this week and compare it with the last normal round, so the blind hours become visible.
Give one night shift person one fixed check time and one log page for chamber and power status, so overnight problems are noticed sooner.

problems.words: Temperature logs are filled in at the end of the week
quick_ideas: Make the log a shift task with a time beside each entry, so gaps are visible
Check the log yourself at random times.

workzap_build.text: A temperature and power log filled hourly by staff on phone, warning you right away if an entry is missed.

problems.free_stops: Log intervals and flags are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Look at last week's log pages and count entries written in the same handwriting block, so you see how often records are filled late.
Make one supervisor collect each shift log at handover into one folder, so missing entries are caught the same day.

problems.words: Diesel for generators during load shedding is killing margins
quick_ideas: Note generator hours beside each fill, so you can see diesel against actual running
Record load-shedding hours for a week.

workzap_build.text: A diesel and generator-hours log with cost per chamber per month.

problems.ask_first: What backup do you use when power goes?
problems.free_stops: How costs are split by chamber is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write generator running hours and load shedding hours side by side for this week, so you can see when fuel use rises beyond outages.
Give one person one page for every generator fill and running period, so diesel discussions start from one current record.

problems.words: Brands we store for want daily stock reports, we send them by hand
quick_ideas: Agree one fixed report format with each brand, so it isn't rebuilt each time
Prepare it at one fixed time daily.

workzap_build.text: A daily stock report emailed to each brand client, created from the same inward and outward records.

problems.ask_first: How many brand clients want reports?
problems.free_stops: Report contents and delivery are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many times yesterday's stock report was corrected before sending, so you see where daily reporting effort is actually going.
Give one staff member one notebook page per brand for daily opening, movement and closing figures, so hand reports go out faster and more consistently.

never_say: Advice on refrigeration engineering, ammonia or refrigerant handling, or storage temperatures for any product.
Advice on food or pharma storage compliance, insurance claims, contract law or abandoned goods.
Any help altering temperature logs, backdating gate passes, releasing stock improperly or hiding stock from tax or customs.
Assigning blame in client loss disputes.
Storing clients' or labourers' names, CNICs, trade licences or phone numbers.

sample_reply.person: Aloo ka cold store hai Okara ke paas. Har saal zameendar boriyan kam hone ki shikayat karte hain, koi solution hai?
sample_reply.pi:
Bilkul, is ka hal mumkin hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, maal andar aate waqt ginti zameendar ya unke numainde ke saamne karein aur dono dastakhat karein, taake shuruaati adad pe ittefaq ho.
Doosra, har nikasi pe baqi boriyon ka adad usi waqt bata dein.
Pakke hal ke liye Workzap ye banwa sakta hai: har aamad aur nikasi ka record, code wali raseed, aur har dafa zameendar ko WhatsApp pe baqi balance.
